description: DRAFT industry rubric pack WAREHOUSE_LOGISTICS: HIRA calibration v2 evaluation fixtures for an Indian FMCG / e-commerce distribution centre. 5 activities: 2 low-hazard (WH-01, WH-02) and 3 high-hazard (WH-03..WH-05). Same structure as tests/eval/hira_calibration/activities.json: for DRAFT activities the per-hazard likelihood/severity are what an uncalibrated LLM (the v1 Copilot) proposed, often over-stated; recommendedControls are the controls it proposed. Hazards are seeds for the HSE lead to validate. 'expected' is an HSE judgement still to be made ('TODO(HSE lead)'); it must not be fitted to engine output.

STD_5X5.note: Standard 5x5, frequency-anchored likelihood, MODERATE tolerable with ALARP.

JSL_QSD24_GT.note: JSL Hisar plant method QSD/24 (GT > 3.33 significant): plant-index likelihood, MODERATE not acceptable.

activities.title: Manual case picking from ground and first-level racking
activities.activity: Picking cartons (5-20 kg) from floor-level pallet locations and the first rack beam onto a picking trolley against WMS pick lists in the distribution centre

hazards.name: Lifting cartons from floor-level pallets
hazards.consequence: Picker lifts 15-20 kg cartons from floor-level pallets about 400 times a shift: lower-back strain

hazards.name: Bending and twisting at the pick face
hazards.consequence: Repeated bending to pallet base level and twisting to place cartons on the trolley: chronic low-back pain

hazards.name: Box cutter while opening cartons
hazards.consequence: Box-cutter blade slips while opening outer cartons for each-picking: hand laceration

hazards.name: Reach truck entering the pick aisle
hazards.consequence: Picker stepping out of a pick face is struck by a reach truck turning into the aisle: leg fracture or crush injury

hazards.name: Stretch film and pallet debris in aisles
hazards.consequence: Trip on discarded stretch film or a broken pallet board in the pick aisle: sprain

existingControls.description: Pick aisles closed to reach trucks during picking waves by chain barriers at both ends
existingControls.verificationMethod: Wave-start checklist in the WMS signed by the shift lead

existingControls.description: Heavy SKUs (> 15 kg) slotted at waist height; slotting reviewed monthly
Self-retracting safety cutters issued in place of open blades
Waste stretch film collected in aisle-end bins every 2 hours
Safety shoes, high-visibility vest, cut-resistant gloves

recommendedControls.description: Manual handling training
Height-adjustable picking trolleys / pallet lift tables
Job rotation between picking and packing
Back support belts
5S of picking aisles

activities.title: Packing, tape sealing and labelling at the packing stations
activities.activity: Packing e-commerce orders into cartons, sealing them on the automatic carton sealer or with hand tape dispensers, and labelling them at the packing stations

hazards.name: Carton sealer drive belts
hazards.consequence: Packer's fingers drawn between the side drive belts of the automatic carton sealer while pushing an under-filled carton through: finger crush or fracture

hazards.name: Tape dispenser blade
hazards.consequence: Cut from the serrated blade of the hand tape dispenser or the sealer's tape knife: finger laceration

hazards.name: Repetitive packing at a fixed-height table
hazards.consequence: Repetitive folding, taping and labelling of about 600 orders a shift at a fixed-height table: wrist and shoulder strain

hazards.name: Cartons and strapping around the station
hazards.consequence: Trip over flat-pack cartons and strapping around the packing station: sprain or bruise

recommendedControls.description: Guards at the carton sealer drive belts with an emergency stop
Height-adjustable packing tables
Cut-resistant gloves
Training
Housekeeping checklist at every packing station

activities.notes: Only baseline PPE recorded: packing staff supplied by a manpower agency.

activities.title: Forklift and reach-truck traffic in shared aisles and the cross-dock
activities.activity: Moving pallets with 2.5 t electric forklifts and reach trucks between the inbound dock, cross-dock lanes and racking aisles shared with pickers and loaders, including battery charging

hazards.name: Forklift - pedestrian interface
hazards.consequence: Picker or loader in a cross-dock lane is struck by a forklift reversing or travelling with a load that blocks the driver's view: crush injury or fatality

hazards.name: Forklift tip-over
hazards.consequence: Forklift turns at speed with the load raised and tips over: driver crushed under the overhead guard

hazards.name: Load falling from the forks
hazards.consequence: Unwrapped cartons slide off a raised pallet during travel onto a pedestrian or the driver: head or shoulder injury

hazards.name: Battery electrolyte at the charging bay
hazards.consequence: Battery electrolyte (sulphuric acid) splashes into the eyes while topping up forklift batteries with water at the charging bay: chemical eye burn

existingControls.description: Pedestrian walkways separated by steel barriers at the cross-dock, with marked crossing points
Blue-spot and red-zone lights, reverse alarm and an 8 km/h speed limiter on every forklift
existingControls.verificationMethod: Daily pre-use checklist in the forklift app; speed limiter tested monthly

existingControls.description: Only licensed, site-authorised drivers (operator card; refresher every 2 years)
existingControls.verificationMethod: Authorisation register audited monthly by the EHS officer

existingControls.description: Seat belt with operator-presence interlock on all counterbalance forklifts
Battery charging bay with eyewash station; single-point battery watering on 6 of 14 trucks
High-visibility vest and safety shoes for everyone on the floor; face shield and PVC gloves at the charging bay

recommendedControls.description: Pedestrian segregation with barriers
Proximity warning system (tags on pedestrians, alarm on the forklift)
Forklift refresher training
Stretch-wrap every pallet before moving
Single-point watering on all forklift batteries
Safety awareness campaign

items: NM-2026-0145: forklift reversed within 1 m of a picker in cross-dock lane 3
IR-2025-412: loader's foot run over by a forklift at the inbound dock (fracture, lost-time injury)

activities.title: Pallet put-away and retrieval in 10 m high-bay racking
activities.activity: Putting away and retrieving 1 t pallets at up to 9 m beam height in selective pallet racking with reach trucks; pickers work in the same aisles at ground level

hazards.name: Racking collapse after upright impact
hazards.consequence: A reach truck strikes a rack upright; the damaged upright later buckles under full 1 t pallet loads and the bay collapses into the aisle: workers in the aisle crushed, multiple fatalities possible

hazards.name: Load falling from a high bay
hazards.consequence: Loose cartons on a pallet being retrieved from the 8 m top beam fall onto a picker walking in the aisle below: head injury or fatality

hazards.name: Reach truck overload at full lift height
hazards.consequence: Reach truck lifts an overweight pallet to the top beam at full reach and tips forward: operator injured and the load falls into the aisle

hazards.name: Climbing the racking
hazards.consequence: Worker climbs the racking or rides on the forks to reach a misplaced carton at 6 m: fall to the floor, fatal

existingControls.description: Upright protectors at aisle entries and end-of-aisle frame barriers
Beam load notices (SWL per level) on every bay
Annual rack inspection by the racking supplier
Reach trucks with load weight display and height pre-selection

recommendedControls.description: Weekly in-house rack inspection with green / amber / red damage tags
Anti-collapse mesh on the back of the high-bay racks
Rack upright protectors
No climbing of racking; order picker or MEWP for high-level access
Training
Damaged pallets not stored above beam level 1

openCapas.text: Unload and replace the 6 red-tagged rack uprights in aisles 14-16

failures: Rack inspection RI-2026-03 (Sep 2026): 6 uprights with red-category damage in aisles 14-16, bays still loaded
items: Rack inspection RI-2026-03 (Sep 2026): 6 uprights with red-category damage in aisles 14-16, bays still loaded

activities.title: Truck loading and unloading at the dock doors
activities.activity: Unloading and loading trucks and 32 ft containers at 12 dock doors with hydraulic dock levellers, battery-operated pallet trucks (BOPT) driven into the trailer, and hand unloading of floor-loaded cartons

hazards.name: Truck drive-away during loading
hazards.consequence: Truck driver pulls away from the dock while a loader and a BOPT are inside the trailer: the BOPT and loader fall 1.2 m from the dock edge, crush injury or fatality

hazards.name: Trailer creep
hazards.consequence: Trailer creeps away from the dock under repeated BOPT braking; the pallet truck wheel drops into the gap between the leveller lip and the trailer bed and the truck tips over with the operator

hazards.name: Dock leveller lip
hazards.consequence: Loader's foot trapped under the dock leveller lip as it lowers onto the trailer bed: crushed foot

hazards.name: Open dock edge with no truck
hazards.consequence: Loader walks backwards pulling a pallet truck off the open dock edge when no truck is docked: 1.2 m fall with the pallet truck, head injury

hazards.name: Hand unloading of floor-loaded containers
hazards.consequence: Loaders hand-unload about 1,200 floor-loaded 20 kg cartons from a 32 ft container: lower-back strain, worse inside a hot container

recommendedControls.description: Wheel chocks at every dock door
Vehicle restraint (dock lock) interlocked with the dock door and traffic lights
Truck keys held by the dock supervisor during loading
Telescopic belt conveyor for floor-loaded containers
Training
Dock edge barrier chain when the door is open with no truck

existingControlProposals.description: Dock SOP WH-SOP-03: truck keys handed to the dock supervisor and wheel chocks placed before the dock door opens
existingControlProposals.verificationMethod: Dock door log signed by the dock supervisor for every truck

openCapas.text: Vehicle restraints (dock locks) with traffic lights interlocked to the dock doors at doors 1-12

items: NM-2026-0377: truck moved off dock door 7 while a loader was inside the trailer, no injury

activities.notes: No controls captured in the draft (dock activity added from scratch by the new 3PL site team); the site SOP register holds one.
